strategies.name: Baseline 8-stage all-reduce cascade
strategies.desc: Directly implements 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved local coupling/decoupling transformations. Each stage performs one all-reduce (8 total dispatches), followed by local element-wise operations that apply or undo bidiagonal coupling. Represents the reference approach with maximum dispatch count but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter + all-gather hierarchical decomposition
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing each rank to compute its own shard's coupling transformation locally between the two collectives. Doubles dispatch count to 16 but reduces per-collective payload size by factor of world_size, potentially improving bandwidth utilization and enabling parallel local computation during the scatter phase.

strategies.name: Pipelined all-reduce with fused coupling
strategies.desc: Fuses the coupling transformation into the reduction operation by creating a custom reduction buffer that carries both the sum and the coupled values. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches but eliminates separate coupling/decoupling passes by maintaining auxiliary state. Trades memory (2x buffer) for reduced local-op overhead between collectives.

strategies.name: Two-level hierarchical with intra-node optimization
strategies.desc: Exploits the multi-node topology by first performing intra-node reductions (assuming multiple ranks per node at world_size=224), then inter-node all-reduce, then intra-node broadcast, repeated for 8 stages. Reduces inter-node bandwidth pressure and leverages faster intra-node interconnect, potentially 24-32 total dispatches but with smaller cross-node payloads.

strategies.name: Butterfly all-reduce with delayed coupling
strategies.desc:
Batches multiple stages together by deferring the coupling/decoupling transformations until after 2-4 consecutive all-reduce operations complete. Performs 8 all-reduces but reorganizes local computation to allow better instruction-level parallelism and cache reuse. Maintains 8 dispatches but increases intermediate buffer requirements and local compute density between collectives.
